name: Schumann 7.83 Hz sine
origin: Popular Schumann-resonance device concept (hypothesis: Cherry 2002); tested in an RCT by Huang et al. 2022 (Chang Gung, Taiwan)
summary: A 7.83 Hz sine for 30 min on all eight ring coils in phase, the popular 'Schumann resonance' relaxation and sleep program. Its health claims are hypotheses or vendor statements; the one RCT of a Schumann sleep device found no between-group difference on polysomnography (Huang 2022). Only the 7.83 Hz comes from the sources: the length and the coil layout are this project's choice.
notes: Huang 2022 put a device by the bed facing the head, on from about 1 h before bed until rising, for 4 weeks, with a composite 7.83 Hz plus theta and delta signal and no stated field strength or distance (p.4 [1116]). Danho 2025 exposed 10 boys to a commercial plasma-tube device (7.83 Hz with harmonics at 14.3, 20.8 and 27.3 Hz) for 60 min once a week for eight weeks, seated about 2 m from the antenna for the first 20 min (p.2-3). The natural Schumann resonance is a field of about 1 pT near 7.8 Hz; its fundamental drifts between about 7.2 and 8.2 Hz over the day. This program is an approximation built from those descriptions: it plays only a 7.83 Hz sine, on all eight ring coils in phase, for 30 min. The 30 min and the eight coils in phase come from no source. Huang's theta and delta parts and Danho's harmonics are not played; lowfield-schumann-783-harmonics adds the higher resonance modes. Huang gives no field. Danho's 0.5 to 1 uT is the value at 1 m from the antenna, taken from a dipole model and 'not directly measured' (p.2-3). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT the helmet is about a million times stronger than the natural resonance, so this is not a 'natural' field. In Huang 2022 'there was no significant difference between the two groups before and after treatment' on polysomnography (p.5 [1117]), and a co-author held the patent licence. Danho's control group sat in the same place with the device off and the antenna hidden: single-blind, not randomised (p.2); the outcome was jump performance. Cherry 2002 proposed health effects via melatonin as a hypothesis. At about 1e-6 V/m induced field there is no credible mechanism. Treat the claims as unproven and test against sham with the app's Blind option. No sleep or health benefit is promised; stop on discomfort.
setting: Evening, lying down in a quiet, dim room; 30-60 min (Huang 2022 ran the device from about 1 h before bed until rising). All eight ring coils in phase, as there is no evidence-based placement.
source: Huang et al. 2022, Nat Sci Sleep https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35707548/ ; Einstein Telescope Schumann-resonance study, arXiv 2110.14730 (SR amplitude about 1 pT) https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.14730 ; Ouyang et al. 2013, Chinese J Geophys 56(3):265-272 (SR modes 7.8, 14.1, 20.3, 26.4, 32.5 Hz) https://html.rhhz.net/Geophy_en/html/20130304.htm ; Cherry 2002, Natural Hazards 26:279 https://ideas.repec.org/a/spr/nathaz/v26y2002i3p279-331.html ; Danho et al. 2025, Cureus https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41080364/
